newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - T-bond vols march upward before ECI.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - T-bond vols march upward before ECI.

text.p: Traders bid up implied volatility for Treasury bond options Monday as the market braced for several potentially earth-shaking U.S. economic reports.
The data barrage begins Tuesday with the release of the second-quarter employment cost index and continues through Friday, when the July employment numbers are reported.
September bond volatility rose to 8.70 percent at the close of trading, up from about 8.45 percent on the opening.
"I think it's going to stay firm through the week," said a bond options floor trader for a U.S. bank.
For second-quarter ECI, analysts on average look for labor expenses to gain 0.8 percent, following a tame 0.6 percent rise in the first quarter.

Traders said many directional trades in bond options continued to reflect a bullish bias, with a number of 1,000-lot-plus call purchases seen. The underlying futures drifted higher through the session to close up 13/32 at 115-14/32, hovering just off the recent 1-1/2-year high.
One trading firm bought 2,000 September 117-00 calls, another bought 1,500 of the calls, and a third house bought 1,000 September 116-00 calls.
One house bought 3,000 September 118-00 calls in combination with the purchase of a 112-00/113-00 put spread.
Early in the session, two dealer firms each purchased 500 "one-by-two" September 116-00/118-00 call spreads, buying the 116-00 calls and selling double the number of 118-00 calls.
Dealers also were sellers of the 117-00 and 118-00 calls, possibly to cover long positions ahead of the data, brokers said.
Toward the close, one brokerage house sold 1,500 September 114-00 puts.
Eurodollar volatilities were steady to slightly higher, with December unchanged at 9.0 percent and March up 0.2 percentage point at 11.2 percent.
A Eurodollar options broker said the impending data effectively quelled trading activity, though short-dated August 94.00 calls saw healthy turnover.
A one-by-two put spread in short-dated September options was the day's feature. A U.S. banking firm bought 2,000 puts in the 93.75 strike and sold twice the amount of 94.00 puts.
